root_cause.text: The DAMON core does not validate the user-provided node ID (nid) before using it in node memory macros (NODE-DATA()), enabling an out-of-bounds memory access when an invalid node ID (e.g., -1) is supplied.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message explicitly state that "Users can set damos_quota_goal->nid with arbitrary value... DAMON core is using those for NODE-DATA() without a validation of the value. This can result in out of bounds memory access." The patch adds a check using `invalid_mem_node(goal->nid)` to handle invalid IDs, and the provided user-space example with `-1` triggers a kernel paging request.
